loci.name: allreduce-ceiling-and-definition
loci.one_line: What all-reduce bandwidth can DDP actually get on this box: is 0.75 GiB/s the structural Gen2-x4 host-staged ceiling, what does the number even measure (algbw, busbw, or aggregate), does BAR1 P2P lift it, and does the 24-capacitor x16 mod multiply it?
loci.rationale: Every overhead number in the repo is comm_time/compute_time, and this locus fixes the numerator. The repo divides by one user-measured number, 0.75 GiB/s (research.md §1-2), and the corpus holds four incompatible measurements of the same quantity: ~1.0 GB/s busbw at Gen2 x4 (lessonsmd, deepseek-v4-cmp170hx/SETTINGS.md); 3.69 / 3.85 / 4.24 GB/s NCCL all-reduce busbw at 256 MiB (club BENCHMARKS) — but readmemd shows that receipt is three cards at Gen2 x16 behind PLX with no BAR1-P2P patch and NCCL SHM transport; BAR1 P2P at 1.68 GB/s each way at Gen2 x4 on 12/12 pairs (bayley/cmpunlocker); and static-BAR1 P2P at 5.79 GB/s on the x16 host (club UNDERSTANDING). Analyst b re-derived a hard ceiling: ring per-rank load 2(N-1)/N = 1.6 at N=5, host-staging doubles PCIe traversal to 3.2x payload, Gen2 x4 measures 1.68 GB/s, so the ceiling is 0.525 GB/s = 0.489 GiB/s — and the repo's 0.805 GB/s sits 1.53x ABOVE it. That is not a rounding error; it means either the fabric is better than assumed (x16, or P2P working) or the number is not algbw. Analyst a adds that P2P is a latency lever, not a bandwidth lever: club UNDERSTANDING measures P2P copy 5.79 GB/s vs host-staged 6.21-6.30 GB/s at 256 MiB, but 16/194 us vs 22/343 us latency. So 'no P2P' costs DDP little (one large all-reduce) and costs TP/FSDP a lot (many small collectives).
loci.key_arithmetic: ring per-rank 1.6 x S; host-staged 3.2 x S; ceiling 1.68/3.2 = 0.525 GB/s = 0.489 GiB/s; repo 0.805 GB/s = 1.53x ceiling. busbw reading -> 3.98 s -> 53.6% overhead at 810 TFLOPS, 27% at 55% MFU; overhead constant 5.4e5 not 3.6e5. aggregate reading -> 168% overhead. algbw reading -> physically impossible.

opposing_positions.position: 0.75 GiB/s is the real x4 host-staged ceiling: no P2P means every byte crosses PCIe twice, and NCCL ring/LL cannot exceed ~1 GB/s busbw at Gen2 x4.
3.69-4.24 GB/s is achievable — the club measures it on a 4-card PLX host; that host runs Gen2 x16, so the gap is link width, not NCCL.
0.75 GiB/s is not physically reachable as algbw on x4 host-staged; the figure must be busbw or aggregate, and the true overhead constant is 5.4e5 tokens, not 3.6e5.
BAR1 P2P works at 1.68 GB/s each way at Gen2 x4 and lifts small-collective latency, but club p2p.md reports the patch hangs every NCCL collective.

loci.why_it_pays_off: It decides whether the capacitor mod is a prerequisite for the whole program, whether 'no P2P' is a bandwidth or only a latency constraint, and whether the repo's 36% DDP overhead is 36%, 54%, or 168%.
loci.what_would_settle_it: A 5-rank nccl-tests all_reduce_perf on the user's x4 box at 1 MB / 100 MB / 1 GB, with and without bf16_compress_hook, reporting BOTH algbw and busbw columns; repeated on a cap-modded x16 card; plus p2pBandwidthLatencyTest with and without the BAR1-P2P patch. The repo must state which column its 0.75 GiB/s came from.

loci.name: topology-cost-at-1m-tokens
loci.one_line: At 1M-token global batches, is DDP really the only viable topology — or does PP beat it once activation hand-offs are overlapped, and is the repo's 'overhead depends only on batch size, not model size' invariance false for MoE?
loci.rationale: This is the query's first named claim and the repo's topology table (research.md §2) is the spine of its recommendation — and it is wrong in at least four ways the corpus exposes. (a) PP cost: the repo treats PP's activation hand-off as an additive 16 GB/step (21 s, ~2.9x overhead), but physical-mods measures PP's inter-card traffic at 10,240 bytes per token per hop for a 5120-hidden model, and lessonsmd / mobius / RoundPipe all describe PP as moving O(activations) that overlaps with compute. At 1M tokens the per-micro-batch hand-off is ~335 MB, which fits inside a 32k-token micro-batch's compute window, so PP's communication is hideable rather than additive; with 30 micro-batches and 5 stages the bubble is ~12%, not fatal. (b) The MoE invariance error: research.md headline #3 states 'DDP's overhead depends only on batch size, not model size — compute and gradient payload both scale with params.' That holds only when total = active, i.e. dense models. The repo's own experiment axis is a sparse MoE at 'up to 7B total / ~1B active' (goal-and-requirements.md). Gradient payload scales with TOTAL trainable params; compute scales with ACTIVE. For 7B-total/1B-active the payload is 14 GB, host-staged ring is 44.8 GB, comm is 26.7 s against 7.41 s of compute — 360% overhead (235% even at the repo's own 0.75 GiB/s), not 36%. The ratio is exactly the total/active ratio, 7x. (c) EP: the repo's ~70x estimate treats EP as ruled out, but ThunderEP measures degraded-but-workable EP and every EP library (DeepEP, NCCL EP, UCCL-EP) requires NVLink/P2P/RDMA — so EP is ruled out for a different reason than the repo gives. (d) TP: the repo is right that TP is the worst option (86 all-reduces per forward on 43 layers; PP beats TP 6.6x on prefill, 5,321 vs 801 tok/s at 77k), but for the wrong reason — it is a latency problem, not a bandwidth one.
loci.key_arithmetic: MoE 7B total / 1B active: payload 14 GB; host-staged ring 44.8 GB -> 26.7 s; compute 7.41 s; overhead 360% (235% at repo's 0.75 GiB/s). Dense 1B: payload 2 GB -> 3.98 s -> 54%. Ratio 7x = total/active ratio. PP hand-off 10,240 B/token/hop; 1M tokens -> ~335 MB/micro-batch vs 1.7-2.8 s compute window; 30 micro-batches / 5 stages -> ~12% bubble.

opposing_positions.position: DDP is the only viable topology: PP's activation traffic is 16 GB/step (2.9x compute), TP runs 86 all-reduces per forward, and EP does two all-to-alls per MoE layer at ~70x compute time.

PP is viable and cheaper than FSDP on a bandwidth-starved fabric: it moves only activations (10,240 B/token/hop), overlaps transfer with compute, and PP+offload beats ZeRO-2/FSDP/Megatron-PP/TP by 1.48-2.16x on 8x4090.
DDP's overhead is invariant to model size because compute and gradient payload both scale with params.

That invariance fails for MoE: per-token FLOPs scale with active params while communication scales with total trainable params, making MoE qualitatively communication-bound rather than a matter of degree.
EP is ruled out by the fabric: every production EP library requires NVLink, P2P, or RDMA, so no-P2P means every byte crosses PCIe twice.

loci.why_it_pays_off: It is the query's first named claim and the repo's PP row is wrong in a direction that changes the recommendation: PP may let 7B train fully without FSDP or frozen tables. The MoE invariance error is the single largest quantitative error in the repo — 360% vs 36% overhead flips MoE from 'cheap' to 'the most expensive arm'.
loci.what_would_settle_it: A per-micro-batch PP hand-off measurement on this box (or a worked 1F1B schedule cost model using the 10,240 B/token/hop figure), a PP-vs-FSDP comparison at equal trainable params and 1M-token batches, and a DDP gradient-buffer measurement on a 7B-total/1B-active MoE confirming the payload is sized by total params.

loci.name: memory-budget-and-frozen-tables
loci.one_line: Re-derive the 64 GB budget from the cited papers: is the frozen table 12B params (24 GB) or 6B (12 GB), do the 32k LM-head logits add 10-20 GB the repo omits, and does 7B fit fully trainable via 8-bit Adam / Adafactor / ZeRO-1-2 — making freezing an architecture choice rather than a necessity?
loci.rationale: This is the direct test of the query's third claim, and the repo's memory table has three unchecked terms plus a missing alternative. (1) Frozen table size: memory-grafting reports 'the top 1M most frequent n-grams per order' across 3 orders = 3M entries per grafted layer, 'roughly 12 GB of frozen memory per layer', and 'approximately 12B frozen grafting memory' for a 0.92B-trainable recipient — 24 GB at bf16, twice the repo's 6B/12 GB, and offloaded rather than resident. research.md §3 transcribes this as '33M entries per grafted layer' while keeping 'roughly 12 GB per layer' — but 33M x 2048 dims x 2 B = 135 GB/layer, a 10x internal inconsistency. (2) Logits: at 32k x 151,669 vocab the LM head produces 9.94 GB bf16 / 19.88 GB fp32, entirely omitted from the repo's 3.2 GB activation estimate. (3) The repo's headline finding #4 says 7B fully trainable needs ~112 GB/card and therefore must freeze 6B params — but three independent routes break that arithmetic: 8-bit Adam cuts optimizer state from 84 GB to ~14 GB (ICLR-2022), Adafactor's O(n+m) state is at most ~4 B/param, and ZeRO-1/ZeRO-2 shard optimizer state across 5 ranks at DDP-identical 2-Psi communication. (4) The paper's own numbers undercut the premise: at 0.92B, vanilla Engram UNDERPERFORMS MoE (45.03 vs 45.62) and grafting recovers only +0.2 to +1.4 after 50B tokens; the 0.92B result used 50B tokens, not 9B. (5) Production memory models train their tables, not freeze them: Engram-27B trains 5.7B Engram params via model-parallel sharding + all-to-all, LongCat-Flash-Lite trains 31.4B n-gram params from scratch, UltraMemV2 trains 120B sparse memory params.
loci.key_arithmetic: Paper: 3M entries x 2048 x 2B = 12.3 GB/layer; 2 layers = 24.6 GB = 12.3B frozen params. Repo's 33M entries -> 135 GB/layer. Logits 32768 x 151669 x 2B = 9.94 GB (fp32 19.88 GB). 1B trainable + 12B frozen: 16 + 24 + 3.2 + 9.9 = 53.1 GB (repo claims 28 GB). 0.92B + 12B: 51.9 GB (repo claims 31 GB). 1.5B + 12B: 61.1 GB (repo claims 35 GB). Offloaded lookup: 5 KB x 2 layers x 135k tok/s = 1.35 GB/s = 80% of the 1.68 GB/s link. 8-bit Adam on 7B: 14 GB weights + 14 GB grads + ~14 GB state = ~42 GB before activations.

opposing_positions.position: Frozen tables are pure VRAM: zero optimizer state, zero per-token FLOPs, so 7B total / 1B trainable fits DDP at ~28 GB/card and is the cheapest capacity available.

Production-scale memory models train their tables: Engram-27B trains 5.7B Engram params via model-parallel sharding + all-to-all, LongCat-Flash-Lite trains 31.4B n-gram params from scratch, UltraMemV2 trains 120B sparse memory params.
7B fully trainable needs ~112 GB/card with Adam (14 weights + 14 grads + 84 state), so DDP on 64 GB is impossible and freezing is required.
7B fits without freezing: 8-bit Adam gives ~42 GB, Adafactor ~28 GB of state, and ZeRO-1/2 shard state at DDP-identical 2-Psi communication.

Frozen Engram at ~1B is not a free win: vanilla Engram underperforms MoE at 0.92B (45.03 vs 45.62) and grafting recovers only +0.2 to +1.4 after 50B tokens, so a 9B-token run will not reproduce the delta.

loci.why_it_pays_off: It decides whether the repo's central design (7B total / 1B trainable) reproduces the paper it cites or is a smaller, offloaded variant that will not show the reported delta — and whether the frozen-table premise is a memory necessity at all. If 7B fits with 8-bit Adam or ZeRO-1/2, the whole frozen-Engram architecture collapses into a choice.
loci.what_would_settle_it: A memory accounting for 7B under 8-bit Adam, Adafactor and ZeRO-1/2 that includes fp32 master weights, 32k activations and fused/chunked cross-entropy logits; Memory Grafting's table-size ablation at 0.92B (entries per layer vs loss delta); and a measured lookup-latency curve for host-side hashing at 3M entries/layer, resident vs offloaded.

loci.name: sustained-throughput-at-32k
loci.one_line: What is the sustained bf16 training throughput per card — 42, 49, 74.6-78.5, 91-100, 155.7, 162, or 164.4-192.7 TFLOPS — and is the repo's 6-FLOPs/param/token model even valid at 32k, where attention's quadratic term is 52-72% of step FLOPs?
loci.rationale: The repo's ~810 TFLOPS aggregate is the denominator of every overhead estimate and the basis of the 80-120k tok/s prediction, and the corpus holds at least six incompatible per-card figures: 42 TFLOPS fp16 on the stock card (exploration-of-cryptocurrency-mining-specific-gpus-in-ai, all-gbs-without-flops); 49.05 TFLOPS in the 170th Street spec sheet; 74.6-78.5 TFLOP/s measured by the club's own health gate; 91-100 TFLOPS/GPU in the repo's proven 494M baseline; 155.7 TFLOPS on a healthy unlocked card vs 39.3 under PWRBRK#; 162 TFLOPS in the repo; 164.4-192.7 in performancemd's unlock table. Analyst b adds a second, independent error on the same denominator: 6ND counts only linear-layer FLOPs. At 32k the quadratic attention term dominates for small models — Qwen3-0.6B (28L, 16Q/8KV, d=128) gives 2.46e14 attention FLOPs against 1.18e14 linear, i.e. attention is 68% of the step and total FLOPs are 3.09x the 6ND estimate. The repo's own 494M baseline is 72% attention, 3.54x 6ND. So the predicted 80-120k tok/s at 32k is 2.1-3.1x optimistic: the 32k/4k per-token FLOP ratio is 2.68x, which turns 140k tok/s into ~52k, or ~39k with +35% activation checkpointing. Analyst a notes the repo's own numbers already contradict its headline: a 500M model at 32k needs ~4.6 GFLOPs/token, so 80-120k tok/s implies 74-110 TFLOPS/card — consistent with the sustained figures and only ~half the 162-TFLOPS headline.
loci.key_arithmetic: Qwen3-0.6B at 32k: attention 2.46e14 vs linear 1.18e14 -> 68% attention, 3.09x 6ND. 494M baseline: 72% attention, 3.54x 6ND. 1B-active/24L/2048: 52% attention, 2.07x 6ND. 32k/4k per-token FLOP ratio 2.68x -> 140k tok/s becomes ~52k, ~39k with +35% checkpointing; repo predicts 80-120k. 500M at 32k = ~4.6 GFLOPs/token -> 80-120k tok/s implies 74-110 TFLOPS/card.

opposing_positions.position: The unlocked card really delivers ~162-192 TFLOPS bf16; the 202.1 ceiling is SM-count scaling from A100 and the repo's 162 is conservative.
The card delivers only ~42-49 TFLOPS fp16; tensor cores are unusable on the stock card and the spec sheet says 49.05 even unlocked.
Real sustained throughput is ~75-100 TFLOPS/card: the club's health gate measures 74.6-78.5 and the repo's own 494M baseline implies 91-100.
6 FLOPs/param/token is the right denominator for the throughput model.
6ND omits the quadratic attention term, which at 32k is 52-72% of step FLOPs for 0.5-1B models, making the throughput prediction 2-3x optimistic.

loci.why_it_pays_off: It fixes both the numerator (TFLOPS) and the denominator (FLOP accounting) of the overhead model and the wall-clock feasibility of every experiment. The corpus has the numbers but no training-shaped measurement, and the repo's headline and its own throughput estimate contradict each other.
loci.what_would_settle_it: A training-shaped bf16 benchmark at 32k on one unlocked card — e.g. a 100-step 500M-model smoke test — reported as sustained TFLOPS/GPU and MFU, with and without activation checkpointing, plus a measured 32k-vs-4k tok/s ratio to test the quadratic-term correction.

loci.name: csa2-at-32k-sm80
loci.one_line: Is CSA2 trainable at 32k on GA100 within 64 GB — or is the indexer's score-tensor memory and SM90-only kernel path a hard blocker, and is a block-sparse family (MoBA/NSA) the better experiment?
loci.rationale: The repo's CSA2 verdict ('worth one experiment, most likely to disappoint at 32k') is right for the wrong reasons, and the corpus contains a hard feasibility blocker the contradiction graph only partly surfaces. (a) The indexer, not attention, gates sequence length: the materialized [B,S,HI,T] FP32 score tensor is 64 GB at S=32,768 with V4-Flash dimensions and peaks at 129 GB on a 140 GB H200 (streamindex); the reference implementation materializes 68.7 GB at 32k/H_q=16, already over a 64 GB card (dsa_reference.py). (b) The chunked partition-merge top-k fix runs at 0.40 GB and is 10.3x faster at 32k, but it is a Triton research driver, and the production DSA kernels are SM90/SM100-only — dsa_reference.py is the only SM80-runnable path. (c) The repo's reasoning is inverted: it says the 16,384 candidate cap 'barely binds' at 32k, but a cap of 16,384 positions against a 32k sequence binds 2x, so the sparsity is real. (d) The payoff is granularity-dependent: LongCat measures 0.83x total vs dense MLA at 32K — sparse is a net LOSS at 32K, with crossover at 64K — while block-granular families (NSA, MoBA, HySparse2) win. (e) The repo's per-layer-indexer cost model overstates by ~10x: V4.1's real layer mix is 4 Full / 4 Reindex / 27 Reuse / 2 SWA, so 67.5% of layers run no indexer at all.
loci.key_arithmetic: Indexer score tensor [B,S,HI,T] FP32 at S=32768, V4-Flash dims = 64 GB; measured peak 129 GB on H200; chunked partition-merge = 0.40 GB, 10.3x faster. dsa_reference.py at 32k/H_q=16 = 68.7 GB. Candidate cap 16,384 vs S=32,768 -> 2x binding, not 'barely'. LongCat at 32K: 0.83x total vs dense MLA. V4.1 layer mix 4/4/27/2 -> 67.5% indexer-free.

opposing_positions.position: CSA2 is worth one experiment at 32k: the published 890 B/token KV cache and near-flat decode FLOPs are real, and the 16,384 cap gives some sparsity even at 32k.
CSA2 is not runnable at 32k on this box: the indexer score tensor is 64-129 GB at 32k, the reference path needs 68.7 GB, and every production DSA kernel is SM90/SM100-only.
Sparse attention at 32k is granularity-dependent and mostly a loss unless block-granular: LongCat measures 0.83x total vs dense MLA at 32K with crossover at 64K, while NSA/MoBA/HySparse2 win.
The 16,384 candidate cap barely binds at 32k, so CSA2's sparsity is marginal.
A 16,384 cap against a 32,768 sequence binds 2x, so the repo's reasoning is inverted even though its verdict may hold.

loci.why_it_pays_off: It converts 'does CSA2 pay off' into 'is CSA2 runnable on sm_80 at all', which is a go/no-go for the experiment rather than a judgment call. It also supplies the payoff ceiling: a 2x attention win is worth 26-36% of step time at 32k, which is the most any sparse-attention arm can buy.
loci.what_would_settle_it: A runnable sm_80 chunked-indexer path (StreamIndex or equivalent) benchmarked at 32k on a 64 GB card, plus a 32k training loss comparison against dense MLA and a MoBA 90/10 hybrid at equal token budget.

loci.name: token-budget-and-effect-size
loci.one_line: Are 9B tokens enough to resolve the architecture deltas the program wants to measure, when every published ablation at comparable scale used 50-350B tokens and the corpus disagrees on whether architecture changes per-token efficiency at all?
loci.rationale: The contradiction graph has no cluster on this, and it is the quietest feasibility constraint in the whole program. The repo's plan is 9B tokens at ~500M active params (18 tokens/param, near Chinchilla-optimal) and ~25 h at 100k tok/s. But every architecture result the program wants to reproduce was measured at a much larger budget: Memory Grafting trains 0.92B for 50B tokens and 2.8B for 100B; periodic-weak-spots trains a Qwen3-0.6B backbone for 100B; analysing-the-impact-of-sequence-composition trains 1.3B for 150B; SmolLM2 uses 350B tokens per ablation at 1.7B; MoBA uses 30B at 1.5B for its 32K hybrid; NSA uses 260-270B at 27B. So 9B is 3-39x short. Worse, the corpus disagrees on whether the axis matters at all: cramming says architecture does not change per-token efficiency at fixed parameter count; over-tokenized-transformer says input-vocabulary scaling at 400M matches a 2.5x larger model and gives a 5.7x loss speedup at 1B; memory-grafting says vanilla Engram is NEGATIVE at 0.92B (-0.59 vs MoE) and grafting only +0.2 to +1.4 after 50B tokens. A 9B-token run therefore risks a null result that cannot be distinguished from an underpowered one.
loci.key_arithmetic: 9B = 25 h at 100k tok/s; 100B = 11.6 d; 150B = 17.4 d; 350B = 40.5 d; five arms at 100B = ~58 GPU-days. Chinchilla: 400M -> 8.0B tokens, 1B -> 20.2B tokens, so 9B is 45% of optimal for 1B active.

opposing_positions.position: Architecture does not change per-token efficiency at fixed parameter count; only throughput matters, so a 9B-token comparison of MoE/Engram/CSA2 against a dense control will land within noise.
Memory-axis changes are first-order quality levers even at small scale: input-vocabulary scaling at 400M matches a 2.5x larger model and gives a 5.7x loss speedup at 1B.
The memory axis's benefit is scale- and budget-dependent and can be negative at ~1B: vanilla Engram underperforms MoE at 0.92B, and grafting recovers only +0.2 to +1.4 after 50B tokens.

loci.why_it_pays_off: It decides whether the experiment program can detect the deltas it is designed to measure, and it changes the recommended token budget and wall-clock plan. A null result at 9B is uninterpretable, which is the worst outcome for a program whose purpose is to settle these questions.
loci.what_would_settle_it: A token-budget sweep or scaling-law fit showing when the Engram/CSA2 delta exceeds run-to-run noise, plus the wall-clock cost at the measured sustained throughput.
